# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

## Threshold point: the Seller's "[STANDARD]" labels and "Reviewer Efficiency Note"

The Seller marks most clauses "[STANDARD]" and says they have been "reviewed and cleared by both sides." It also says the Buyer has "already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package." **I have disregarded this.**

- It is the counterparty's own characterisation, in an untrusted draft.
- Nothing in the record shows the Buyer agreed to any of these positions.
- Most "[STANDARD]" items conflict directly with our playbook.
- The Seller's covering email itself invites "your mark-up."

Every clause below has been reviewed on its merits. We should reject the labels and the "proceed on that basis" premise in writing, so silence is not later argued as acceptance.

---

## Issue-by-issue review

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap (cl 12.1)
- **Seller:** 20% of price (AUD 4,800,000).
- **Buyer wants:** 25% (AUD 6,000,000). The 20% fallback requires prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying this draft. None has been given.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; counter at 25% / AUD 6,000,000.** *Reason: the Seller has opened at our unauthorised fallback, and we cannot concede it without Amelia Frost's written sign-off.*

### SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket (cl 12.2)
- **Seller:** de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; only the excess is recoverable (deductible).
- **Buyer wants:** de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; Seller liable from the first dollar once the basket is exceeded (tipping basket).
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; restore AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000 with a tipping basket.** *Reason: the Seller's figures are 5x our thresholds, and the deductible structure permanently removes the first AUD 250,000 of loss.*

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit (cl 12.3 / 13)
- **Seller:** 18 months. It also proposes that "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months after Completion. 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost's written approval (none given). The limitation must apply to general Warranty Claims only.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; restore 24 months and delete the "applies to all Claims" sweep.** *Reason: 18 months is unauthorised, and the sweep silently imports general limits into fundamental, tax, indemnity and fraud claims.*

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental / Title regime
- **Seller:** capacity and title warranties sit under the same caps and time limits as general warranties, "for administrative simplicity."
- **Buyer wants:** a separate regime with:
  - a 100% cap;
  - a claims period of at least six years;
  - no application of the general basket, de minimis or knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; insert a stand-alone Fundamental Warranties regime.** *Reason: title and capacity go to whether we receive what we pay AUD 24m for, and "simplicity" does not justify capping that at 20%.*

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)
- **Seller:** limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to "all Claims of any nature." There is no fraud carve-out, so fraud is captured by implication.
- **Buyer wants:** fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. This is non-waivable under our playbook.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; insert an express overriding fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct carve-out.** *Reason: this is a non-negotiable playbook position, and "of any nature" is drafted to reach fraud.*

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope (Schedule 7; Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2)
- **Seller:** general disclosure of the entire data room (as at 5pm 22 Sep 2026), the Accounts, the statutory registers and publicly searchable records.
- **Buyer wants:** specific fair disclosure only. No whole-data-room, public-register or deemed disclosure.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject paras 1.1–1.2; permit only specific, fair disclosures against identified warranties.** Paras 2–10 can be assessed as specific disclosures. Para 1.4 (no admission) is acceptable only if it does not undermine the specific disclosures. *Reason: general disclosure moves diligence risk onto the Buyer and empties the warranties.*

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier (cl 8.3)
- **Seller:** no claim for anything the Buyer *or its advisers* knew, including matters "discoverable" from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer wants:** the blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion deleted. Any knowledge qualifier must:
  - be limited to named Seller knowledge persons, after reasonable enquiry;
  - never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation:** **Delete cl 8.3.** *Reason: it is an anti-sandbagging bar that, combined with "discoverable," would defeat claims on the very matters we have flagged in diligence.*

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3)
- **Seller:** reasonable endeavours; the condition is "satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent." The Disclosure Letter (para 2) confirms that no final consent and no evidence of satisfaction of the cl 11.3 conditions is in the data room.
- **Buyer wants:** before Completion, an effective consent **and** evidence that its cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied. Consent-on-delivery and reasonable endeavours alone are not enough.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; make an effective, unconditional (or conditions-satisfied) Bluefen consent a Completion condition, with supporting evidence.** *Reason: Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m, about 30% of FY26 revenue, which is material customer risk that must be resolved before we pay.*

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7)
- **Seller:** facility of ~AUD 3.2m outstanding, to be dealt with by a release "provided following Completion." Disclosure para 3 confirms it is not repaid and no discharge is available.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - a current payout letter;
  - direct repayment from Completion funds;
  - effective security releases (cl 9.2 discharge) delivered at Completion.
  
  A post-Completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable undertaking **and** Amelia Frost's approval (not given).
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; require a payout letter, a funds-flow line paying Riverlark directly, and executed releases or discharges at Completion.** *Reason: without them we would buy a company with live security and change-control exposure on an unpaid facility.*

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses (funds flow; DD-005)
- **Seller:** the AUD 420,000 Completion bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and are not itemised. Disclosure para 5 is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs.
- **Buyer wants:** the AUD 420,000 plus any triggered on-costs either shown as a specific line item (Transaction Expense/Debt-like deduction) or expressly Seller-funded. They must not be silently excluded.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the current funds flow.** Either:
  - add an explicit line for the AUD 420,000 plus on-costs, or
  - include a Seller-funding obligation with an indemnity.
  
  Request confirmation of the on-cost quantum (not yet established). *Reason: if the Company pays them post-Completion, the cost falls on the Buyer.*

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity (cl 11.1; DD-004 / DD-010)
- **Seller:** the existing indemnity, limited to the SOW3 payment, is "adequate."
- **Buyer wants:** a broader indemnity covering losses from any failure of SOW3 Project Materials to vest, and related IP claims. The SOW3 cure route (cleared payment, then transfer under cl 7.3) must be preserved. A confirmatory assignment should be sought.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject as drafted; broaden the indemnity and require payment evidence plus a confirmatory IP assignment.** *Reason: the AUD 180,000 open figure in DD-010 is not independently verified either way, and title to the IP, not just the fee, is at stake.*

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Sch 6; DD-006)
- **Seller:** a "preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material."
- **Facts as disclosed:** a download link went to an unintended external address. About 1,240 records may be affected. Access, scope and any notification duty are unestablished.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - log preservation;
  - a completed investigation;
  - regular updates to the Buyer up to Completion;
  - appropriate warranty/indemnity protection.
  
  We make no assumption of a confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or loss figure, in either direction.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not accept the "not material" characterisation. Add pre-Completion covenants on preservation, investigation and updates, with a specific indemnity framework.** *Reason: the facts are unresolved, so the Seller's materiality conclusion is unsupported, though we should not overstate the matter either.*

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (DD-008 / DD-011)
- **Seller:** three related renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000) are "ordinary-course operating costs."
- **Buyer wants:** an assessment of whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or genuinely ordinary course. There should be no automatic Debt classification or price deduction, and no automatic acceptance of the Seller's label.
- **Recommendation:** **Hold the position open and request the contracts, timing, termination rights and accrual treatment.** *Reason: the disclosure itself says these points are not stated, so neither side's classification is established.*

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:**
  - cl 12.3 sweeps "all Claims";
  - cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 apply to "all Claims of any nature";
  - title is merged into the general regime;
  - tax and IP are "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer wants:** Title, Tax, IP, payment obligations and covenants kept as separate categories, each with its own regime. No hidden general-regime override.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the sweeping language.** Define each category, state expressly which limitations apply to each, and add a "specific regime prevails" clause. *Reason: the combined effect of these clauses collapses every protection into the 20% / 18-month general package.*

### SPA-N-015: Title verification (DD-012)
- **Seller:** title to 100% of the shares is "evidenced" by the Company share register at DD-012. Disclosure para 10 admits this is only the source relied on, and that it does not reflect Buyer verification.
- **Buyer wants:** independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority. This includes:
  - ASIC searches;
  - a PPSR search over the shares and Seller;
  - original or certified share certificates;
  - Seller constitution and board approvals;
  - confirmation of no options, rights or encumbrances.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject reliance on DD-012 alone; require independent title evidence as a Completion deliverable, backed by the Fundamental regime (SPA-N-004).** *Reason: an internal register supplied by the Seller is not independent proof of unencumbered title.*

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** tax and IP warranty positions are "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer wants:** tax and IP treated as **OPEN**. There is no resolution, and no assumption of unlimited liability in either direction.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the "settled" characterisation and record tax and IP as open items for separate negotiation.** *Reason: nothing has been agreed, and treating them as settled would quietly subject them to the general cap and time limit.*

---

## Other disclosure items (no action requested, noted for completeness)
- **Office lease (DD-007):** a notification obligation only, not described as a consent requirement. Confirm the notice mechanics and timing.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** an assignment restriction that does not state consent is triggered by a share sale. Confirm no change-of-control trigger elsewhere in the contract.

## Escalation and approvals
- **No fallback is currently authorised.** The 20% cap (N-001), the 18-month period (N-003) and any post-Completion Riverlark release (N-009) each require Amelia Frost's prior written approval. If the deal team wants to use any of them, request her authority, referencing this draft (SPA-003 / Seller Update).
- **Fraud carve-out (N-005):** non-waivable. Nobody on the team can concede it.

## Suggested next step
Send a mark-up restoring all playbook positions. Include a covering note that:
- rejects the "[STANDARD]/cleared" characterisation;
- reserves all rights on every clause.
